gloss: trifling errand; small bit of business

definitions.gloss: trifling errand; small bit of business; minor task
definitions.explanation: A vague, self-deprecating way to refer to an errand or task one needs to attend to, without specifying the details. Often used as a polite excuse to avoid explaining what one is doing.

examples.japanese: ⟦ちょっと→ちょっと：00595_chotto⟧{野暮用|やぼよう}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦ありまして→ある：00006_aru⟧。
examples.english: I have a little errand to run.

examples.japanese: {野暮用|やぼよう}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{外出|がいしゅつ}→外出：02543_gaishutsu⟧し⟦なければならない→なければならない：27600_nakerebanaranai⟧。
examples.english: I need to go out on a small errand.
"Where are you going?" "Just a little errand."

notes:
USAGE:
{野暮用|やぼよう} is used when someone wants to mention they have something to do without going into detail. It is self-deprecating — the speaker downplays the importance of their task. It is a convenient way to politely decline an invitation or excuse oneself.

ETYMOLOGY:
From ⟦{野暮|やぼ}→野暮：06072_yabo⟧ (unsophisticated, uncool) + ⟦{用|よう}→〜用：09842_you⟧ (business, errand). The idea is that the errand is too mundane or unglamorous to be worth mentioning.

SIMILAR WORDS:
⟦{用事|ようじ}→用事：01520_youji⟧ is a neutral term for errands or things to do. {野暮用|やぼよう} adds the nuance of something minor that the speaker prefers not to elaborate on.
